meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

подумать.gloss: to think (for a while), to think it over

meanings.en: to think (for a while), to think it over
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (for a while), to think it over', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'щаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to communicate, to talk with'.

examples.trans: I am not allowed to talk with you.

examples.text: Мне с вами вообще общаться нельзя. Всего доброго.
examples.trans: I'm not allowed to talk to you at all. Good day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'сориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to quarrel, argue', paired with 'поссориться'.

examples.text: И теперь они из-за меня ссорятся.
examples.trans: And now they are fighting because of me.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to divide, share'.

examples.trans: What could we possibly have to fight over?
Have you taken a look at yourself?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to submit, file; to serve', paired with 'подавать'.

examples.text: Ирина Петровна, скажите, пожалуйста. Кандидат Самсонов подал подписи с нарушениями, ведь да?
examples.trans: Irina Petrovna, tell me, please. Candidate Samsonov submitted his signatures with violations, isn't that right?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'salt' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Onion, salt, pepper — and that's all.

examples.text: Попробуй! Лук, соль, перец — и всё.
examples.trans: Try it! Onion, salt, pepper — and that's all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'against', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Все в городе хотят этот кластер. Только ты против.
examples.trans: Everyone in town wants this cluster. Only you are against it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'праздновать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to celebrate'.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет отпраздновать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to celebrate without a reason.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'веркать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sparkle, flash'.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет сверкать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to sparkle without a reason.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('winter, wintry').

examples.trans: He is afraid of the winter forest.

examples.text: Смотри, дядя Даня, видишь, побелел! Испугался он зимнего леса.
examples.trans: Look, Uncle Danya has gone pale, see! He is afraid of the winter forest.

examples.text: Поехали скорее со мной на зимнее озеро.
examples.trans: Come quickly with me to the winter lake.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'the Moon' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Well, you can see the Moon too.

examples.text: Ночью на небе светит полная луна.
examples.trans: At night the full moon shines in the sky.

examples.text: Он же не в квартире, он на улице! Так вы и Луну видите.
examples.trans: But it's not in the flat, it's outside! Well, you can see the Moon too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'well done; good person' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I see, I see, you're a hero. Well done.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be rejected as defective'.

related.gloss: to to be rejected as defective (prefixed perfective)
not to to be rejected as defective (negated infinitive)

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет браковаться без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to be rejected as defective without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'nowhere', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, мне совсем негде жить в Москве.
examples.trans: Yes, I have nowhere to live in Moscow at all.
I have nowhere to spend this night.
Do you have nowhere to live?
